_comment: Values transcribed from Diouf et al. (2026), CMC 87(3), DOI 10.32604/cmc.2026.077139. These are the PAPER's numbers (security-bug target on their dataset). They are ALWAYS labelled 'Paper' in UI/reports and are NEVER our results. Do not edit except to fix a transcription error against the PDF.

paper.title: Predicting Software Security Bugs Using Machine Learning and Quality Metrics: An Empirical Study

dataset.note: Table 11 reports non-buggy as 305,148 but 338,442-33,294=305,148; some tables imply 305,149. Documented as a reporting slip in PAPER_REVIEW.md item 9.

rq3_table15._note: Mean over 5 time-series folds. F1 values for the SVMs are internally inconsistent with their P/R (see PAPER_REVIEW item 1); kept verbatim as the paper reported them.

rq2_thresholds_table14._note: warning / critical thresholds for the paper's core metrics (security-bug target). Our thresholds are computed from OUR dataset in RQ2 and shown separately.

hyperparameters_table4._note: Used EXACTLY in the replication track (RQ3). Global seed 42 elsewhere; LR keeps the paper's random_state=0.

rq1_core_metrics._note: The paper's 6 consensus 'core' metrics (intersection of top-10 importance lists). Used as the comparison target for OUR RQ1 consensus.
rq1_core_metrics.caveat: Exact 6-metric list should be verified against the PDF in Phase 3 before comparison; CountLineCode is provisional.
